name: layonara
description: Differences James approved for the round trip of Layonara's haks (MDL pipeline Phase 2, 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-11). Each entry names a check in runner/approvals.py; a MUST finding is approved only when that check's condition holds on the mesh or node it is about. Approved findings are reported apart, never dropped.

approvals.description: The stored vertex count differs only because the original holds duplicate vertices that the game's compiler merges.
approvals.condition: On the mesh: every compiled triangle is paired, in order, with one of the original's; every paired corner keeps position, UV0-3, normal, tangent and handedness, colour, skin weights, dangly constraint and face material; the vertex streams are the same; and the compiled vertex count equals the number of distinct vertices the original draws by the merge key, floats compared exactly (for an AABB walkmesh, whose merge keeps some equal vertices apart, the corner match alone). Approves the mesh's vertex_count finding.

approvals.description: Faces whose corners merge into one vertex are deleted, as the game's compiler does; the original drew them with zero area.
approvals.condition: On the mesh: every original triangle the compile does not draw has zero area (two corners at the same position), every other one is paired in order with a compiled triangle and matches it corner for corner as for vertex-layout, the triangle and face counts differ by exactly the dropped triangles. Approves the mesh's triangles and face_count findings, and the per-corner findings that only the runner's in-order comparison shows (a dropped face shifts the triangles after it).

approvals.description: The original's tangent stream holds NaN, infinite or zero vectors; the compile writes a generated tangent there.
approvals.condition: On the mesh: as for vertex-layout, except that a paired corner's tangent or handedness may differ when the original's tangent at that corner is NaN, infinite or zero; every differing tangent or handedness corner is such a corner. Approves the mesh's tangent, handedness and vertex_count findings.

approvals.description: The original has no tangent stream and a normal-mapped material; the compile bakes tangents, as the game's compiler does, and clones vertices for them.
approvals.condition: On the mesh: the original has no tangent stream and the compile has one (with handedness), no other stream differs, and every paired corner matches as for vertex-layout. Approves the mesh's vertex_count finding.

approvals.description: 1.69 water meshes use the texture animation slots for a bump-map stream, which ASCII has no place for.
approvals.condition: On the mesh: the original sets texture animation slots (0, 1, 2 or 4) and its slot-3 stream is read as a bump-map stream, not tangents; the compile has none of these; no other stream differs, and every paired corner matches as for vertex-layout. Approves the mesh's vertex_count finding.

approvals.description: A 32-character node name (older tools filled the field with no NUL) is stored as its first 31 characters, as the game's compiler does.
approvals.condition: The original's name (or parent name) is 32 characters, the compiled one is its first 31, and no node of the original with another name has that name once cut (a 32-character name the original already used twice is no new collision; 2026-11-11). Approves the node's name or parent finding, and a node tree finding when the compiled tree is the original's with those names cut and nothing else.

approvals.description: Part numbers differ, but no declaration order the game's compiler could be given reproduces both the original's numbers and its tree (N2), or the original was numbered against another supermodel or none (S2, S4), or T1 once its tree comes back. The compile numbers the nodes as the game's compiler numbers its ASCII, and the animations bind to the same named nodes before and after (James, 2026-11-10).
approvals.condition: On the model (runner/nodefacts.py, facts `compile model.nodes`): node names are unique, or nodes that share a name are told apart by their parent and their order among its children of that name (nodefacts.unique_labels; with a supermodel too, its paths walked by name; a shared name that is a parent only in a model with no supermodel and no animations, a child's parent being the latest node of that name before it, fact `duplicate_parents`, 2026-11-11); the original and the compile have the same nodes with the same parents; a supermodel the model names was found; the compile's part numbers are exactly what MDL-NODE-010 (MDL-NODE-020 with the supermodel, walking on through supermodel nodes numbered -1) gives the ASCII's declaration order; no declaration order makes the game's compiler give the original's numbers and stored tree together (nodefacts.reachable, which errs towards reachable); every animation node, in the original and in the compile, is numbered by MDL-NODE-040 against its own model's geometry (the walk matches names, so where geometry siblings share a name every animation node of that path takes the first stored one's number); and no node tree, name, parent or missing-node finding of the model is left unapproved. Approves the model's nodes[X].number and animations[A].nodes[X].number findings. This covers T1 models once the decompiler declares their children so that the sort rebuilds the stored tree (cleanmodels PR #140): their numbers then differ as N2's do. It never approves the T1 tree finding itself (the >16-children shuffle, so no numbers of a model that still has it), numbers a part-number declaration order reproduces (N1, reachable) or the supermodel -1 walk (S3, numbers not by the rule).

approvals.description: The original was compiled against the base game's or an older supermodel, or as if it had none (S1, S2, S4); the compile counts against the supermodel the haks ship, as MDL-NODE-020/030 require (James, 2026-11-10).
approvals.condition: On the model: it names a supermodel and the supermodel was found; the original and the compile have the same number of nodes; the compile's header node count is the supermodel's header count + the model's nodes + 1; the original's count is its own node count (compiled without the supermodel) or more. Approves model.node_count.

approvals.description: Seven creature supermodels in the haks are binaries compiled against an older a_ba with 31 fewer nodes, so their stored header node count is 31 too low (c_bugbeara 193, where its nodes and today's a_ba give 224). Phase 4 converts them to ASCII; the game's compiler (and cleanmodels) then count them anew, and every model using them numbers its own nodes (those outside the supermodel's paths) 31 higher than its original did. Checked with the game's own compiler (nwmain-linux 89.8193.37-17 compilemodel, 2026-11-12) on c_orcchiefb, c_goblinb and c_skel_war01 against the converted chain: node counts and every node number equal cleanmodels' (c_orcchiefb back_plate 258, original 227). The numbers stay consistent with the supermodel that ships with them; `renumbered` already approves most of these models (28 of 29 converted ones); this covers the ones whose original numbers happen to be reachable against the new count (c_orcchiefb). James, 2026-11-12.
approvals.condition: On the model (runner/nodefacts.py, facts `compile model.nodes`): the conditions of `renumbered` (unique names as it defines them, the same nodes and parents, the supermodel found, the compile's numbers exactly what MDL-NODE-010/020 give the ASCII's declaration order against the supermodel the compile found, every animation node numbered by MDL-NODE-040 in both, no tree, name, parent or missing-node finding left), except that a declaration order may also give the original's numbers; and the supermodel chain the compile used (fact `supermodel_chain`, from the supermodel down to the first binary) holds one of the names in `supermodels` as an ASCII model, i.e. converted. Node and animation node numbers only; the header count is `supermodel-count`'s.

approvals.description: The original's animation header holds a node count that is not the size of the animation's own tree (A2: a_ba's walk, 57 for 55 nodes); the compile writes the tree size (James, 2026-11-10).
approvals.condition: On the animation: the original's header count differs from the number of nodes in its animation tree, the compile's equals the number in its own, both trees have the same number of nodes and the same node names. Approves animations[A].node_count.

approvals.description: nwnmdlcomp left some children out of transparency order (T2); the game's compiler sorts every ASCII, so no ASCII reproduces the stored order, and the compile sorts them as the game would (a draw-order change; James, 2026-11-10).
approvals.condition: On the model: node names are unique; the original and the compile have the same nodes with the same parents; the compiled tree is exactly the original's stored tree with MDL-NODE-012's sort (libstdc++'s std::sort with the transparency comparison, nodefacts.engine_sort) applied to each node's children; and every node whose children differ between the two held them out of the comparison's order in the original (no declaration order gives them). Where such a node has more than 16 children, std::sort also moves equal ones; that is the same sort of the same stored order, and approved with it. Approves nodes.tree. Never the >16-children shuffle of children already in order (T1).

approvals.description: An aabb inner node's plane differs where its children's box centres tie on the two largest axes, so float rounding picks the axis; either splits the boxes equally (Q4; James, 2026-11-10).
approvals.condition: On the aabb node: the two trees have the same entries, boxes (within 1e-4) and faces, and the same inner/leaf shape; every inner entry whose plane differs has, in the original and in the compile, a plane whose axis has |centre delta| within 1e-4 of the largest |centre delta| over x, y and z (the children's box centres, right minus left) and whose sign is that delta's (-Z, 32, for a zero delta); no leaf's plane differs. Approves the node's aabb[j].plane finding (the runner reports the first).

approvals.description: Lost face-neighbour links (category 6), in the second compile: decompiling and compiling the compiled model again changes only which faces the face records name as neighbours. They are read only by the shadow volume (E68), where they change its cost, not the look (James, 2026-11-10).
approvals.condition: On the model: every MUST finding is approved, and every difference between the second compile and the first is of a kind an entry approves (mdlconf.explain_unstable); this entry's kind is the three adjacency fields (s2 at +20, +22, +24) of face records: for the byte-level kinds, the two files are byte for byte the same once those fields are set to zero in both, with the face records the reader finds at the same offsets in both; with dead-face-vertices, the faces' adjacency once the vertices are taken out. Any other difference, vertex order included, leaves the model unstable. Approves the model's instability, reported as the finding `stability binary2`.

approvals.description: The first compile kept vertices of faces it dropped as zero-area (it merges first, then drops, MDL-MESH-020); the ASCII lists no such face, so the second compile leaves out the vertices only those faces used and orders the ones they used first by the faces it keeps (James, 2026-11-10; vertices used first, 2026-11-11).
approvals.condition: On the model: every MUST finding is approved; per mesh, the second compile is the first without the vertices no face or index list of the first uses, and with the vertices at the position of a corner of a zero-area triangle the original draws put where the first compile's face records first use them (every other vertex keeps its order); every dropped or moved vertex is at such a corner; the meshes' boxes, averages and radii are those of their own vertices, except a mesh whose every face the original draws with zero area: the first compile keeps their vertices and no face, the second has no vertices, and that mesh's own box, average and radius are the compiler's for an empty mesh (the model's box stays exact; 2026-11-11); face adjacency may differ (counted, needs unstable-adjacency-only). Meshes are found in the original by their names cut to 31 characters. Every other byte stays exact. Approves the model's instability (`stability binary2`).

approvals.description: The second compile's model bounding box differs from the first's by 1 ulp (float rounding of the sum over the meshes; James, 2026-11-10).
approvals.condition: On the model: every MUST finding is approved; the two compiles are the same length and byte for byte the same except, among the kinds approved, the model bounding box floats (geometry header +136..+159), each by at most 1 ulp. Approves the model's instability (`stability binary2`).

approvals.description: A float is 0.0 in one compile and -0.0 in the other (James, 2026-11-10).
approvals.condition: On the model: every MUST finding is approved; the two compiles are the same length and byte for byte the same except, among the kinds approved, 4-byte fields the reader reads as floats that are 00000000 in one and 00000080 in the other; every other byte stays exact. Approves the model's instability (`stability binary2`).

approvals.description: The original was compiled by a tool that merged meshes' render lists: a receiver's index list also draws copies of other meshes' triangles, and each donor has render 0 and no index list. ASCII has no index lists, so the round trip restores each donor (render 1, drawing with what its copies were drawn with) or folds its copies into the receiver's faces (spec/binary.md, the guidance after MDL-BIN-053). Approved where the whole model draws exactly as before and casts its shadows as before or from what it now draws (James, 2026-11-11, with cleanmodels #141).
approvals.condition: On the model (mdlconf.render_list_facts, `compile model.render_lists`): the original has a receiver (an index list longer than its faces); every triangle the original draws (render != 0, from the index list) and every triangle the compile draws are paired one to one in world space (first keys of position, orientation and scale up the parent chain; corners within 1 mm and 1e-4 in UV0, winding kept; coincident triangles paired by all their attributes first), apart from original triangles of zero area; per pair the drawing mesh's textures 0-3, diffuse, ambient, specular, shininess, transparencyhint, renderhint, tilefade, beaming, rotatetexture, triangle mode, node type and first alpha and selfillumcolor keys are the same, an animation (the model's or its supermodel's) moves or fades the drawing node in both or in neither, and every corner keeps UV1-3, normal, tangent, handedness and colour (a corner whose original tangent is NaN, infinite or zero, or that has tangents only in the compile, needs nan-tangent-fill or tangents-baked); every compiled node that draws a triangle another node drew is a render-0 mesh without an index list in the original (a restored donor), drawing triangles a receiver drew; the shadow faces (shadow or beaming != 0, from the face list) pair the same way with the same shadow, beaming, alpha and animation, except that a restored donor's shadow may follow the alpha it took, and that the faces of a folded donor (render 0 in the compile) may cast no shadow or cast it from a receiver where the receiver now draws them, as many new faces as lost, every one on a triangle the original draws; no node name used twice is a parent or animated; every supermodel is found; no receiver is a skin or animmesh. Approves, on those meshes only, in the decompile and the compile: a restored donor's render, triangles, vertex_count, normal, tangent, handedness and drawing settings (diffuse, ambient, specular, shininess, transparencyhint, renderhint, tilefade, rotatetexture, textures, beaming) and its alpha and selfillumcolor controllers; a folded donor's render, shadow and beaming; a receiver's triangles and vertex_count, and, when it draws folded copies as faces, its face_count and per-corner findings (the in-order comparison shifts); and nodes.tree when the only difference is restored donors re-sorted by the transparencyhint they took (the ASCII's declaration sorted by the original's keys gives the original's children and by the compile's the compile's, for every differing parent). Every other finding of those meshes must pass by its own entry (a restored donor's with its normal, tangent and handedness left out of the corner match), and the mesh is approved all together or not at all.

approvals.description: A chunk emitter's texture field holds bytes an old compiler left there (uninitialised memory such as ff ff ff ff); no ASCII can hold them, and a chunk emitter draws its chunk model, not the texture (James, 2026-11-11).
approvals.condition: On the emitter: its chunk name is not empty, and the original's texture field holds a byte outside 0x20-0x7e before its first NUL. Approves the emitter's texture finding, in the decompile and the compile.

approvals.description: The original's walkmesh tree has more leaves than faces: faces were deleted after it was built (MDL-MESH-024); the compile's tree covers its faces (James, 2026-11-11).
approvals.condition: On the AABB node, in the compile: the original's tree has more leaves than its mesh has faces; the compile's tree is a tree whose leaves name each of its faces once, each leaf's box is its face's box and each inner box the union of its children's (within 1e-4); and the face count is the same in both. Approves the node's aabb entry-count finding.

not_approved.what: face-neighbour (shadow) links, faces.adjacent, in the first compile
not_approved.why: Always a SHOULD finding in the runner, so it never makes a model fail; nothing to approve. In the second compile, see unstable-adjacency-only.

not_approved.what: T1: a node with more than 16 children already in sort order, which std::sort shuffles when the decompiler declares them in stored order; N1: numbers a declaration in part-number order reproduces; S3: the supermodel walk stopping at a supermodel node numbered -1
not_approved.why: Fixable in cleanmodels (decompiler order, supermodel walk), being fixed there; they stay failures (James, 2026-11-10).

not_approved.what: merged render lists whose round trip draws or shadows differently from the original (a triangle lost or added, as plc_candle3 with cleanmodels 83c1922), controller keys, node-pairing artifacts, unstable models whose second compile differs in anything no entry approves (vertex order above all)
